In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: Given a graph G and an integer k, can we distinguish between graphs with few k colorings and those that are not k colorable in polynomial time?
the following question: Given a graph G with a path decomposition with pathwidth pw, is it k colorable and if it is how many proper k colorings does it have?
the following question: Given a graph G, a path decomposition of the graph G of width pw(G), and a number of colors k, can we decide if G is k colorable in (k epsilon)^{pw(G)}poly(n)s time?

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that the Alon Tarsi argument has a new twist that can be used to separate the two classes of graphs in the SETH setting.

there are few cases in which we can prove hardness results for the problem of deciding if a graph admits a coloring with a small number of colors and yet we can still design algorithms for the problem that are fast in practice.
we show that if we can count the number of colorings in a graph, then we can find a coloring in the same time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Alon Tarsi Theorem is more useful than previously believed, and can be used to separate the two cases even if the number of k colorings is not too small, and even if the graph is not regular.
there is hope of using the Alon Tarsi Theorem in the design of algorithms for graph coloring problems, even though there has been no progress in this direction for over a decade.
the number of colorings of a graph is an important property of the graph and it is not always enough to just count the number of colorable graphs.
